title: Repeat-Aware Neighbor Sampling for Dynamic Graph Learning

problem.claim: Dynamic graph learning must model evolving interactions in graphs with time attributes and potentially repeated links between node pairs.

gap.claim: Methods relying mainly on recent neighbor sequences overlook repeat behavior and may fail to accurately capture temporal interaction evolution.

contributions.claim: RepeatMixer incorporates first-order and high-order repeat behavior into neighbor sampling and temporal information learning.

The method defines repeat-aware nodes, constructs repeat-aware neighbor sequences with a sliding window, and uses first- and high-order source and destination sequences for temporal pattern learning through an MLP-based encoder.
A time-aware aggregation mechanism adaptively combines temporal representations from different orders according to the significance of their interaction time sequences.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that RepeatMixer outperforms state-of-the-art models on link prediction tasks.
The authors report that the proposed repeat-aware neighbor sampling strategy is effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic graph learning represents time-varying interactions and repeated links in evolving data scenarios.
Existing approaches primarily use recent neighbor sequences, which neglect repeat behavior and can miss temporal interaction evolution.
RepeatMixer models first-order and high-order repeat behavior through repeat-aware node definitions, sliding-window neighbor sequences, and MLP-based temporal encoding.
Time-aware aggregation combines temporal representations across interaction orders based on their time-sequence significance.
The authors report superior link prediction performance relative to state-of-the-art models.

source_observation.claim: Past repeated interactions between node pairs are described as correlated with future interactions.

interpretation.claim: Temporal interaction models may benefit from explicitly representing repeat behavior instead of relying only on recency.

application.claim: For dynamic relational prediction, include historical repeat-aware structures and assess their value alongside recent-neighbor signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that repeat-aware modeling helps across tasks, datasets, or interaction processes beyond the reported link prediction setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, performance values, or statistical evaluation details.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, scalability, or sensitivity to the sliding-window and aggregation choices.
